title: "John Prine Fingerpicking"
subtitle: "Thumb on alternating bass strings, fingers pinching on 2 and 4"
---

[Open the John Prine Fingerpicking style in the Backing Track](../tools/backing-track.html?style=prine){.btn .btn-outline-primary}

## What it is

A steel-string guitar played with the thumb and fingers at once: the thumb alternates between two bass
strings on every beat while the fingers pluck the chord on the off-beats or pinch with the thumb. No drums,
an upright bass doubling the thumb.

## A little history

Alternating-thumb picking runs back to Black guitarists in the South of the 1920s: Mississippi John Hurt
recorded for OKeh in 1928, and Elizabeth Cotten played *Freight Train* left-handed. In Kentucky, Arnold
Shultz, Ike Everly and Mose Rager handed it to **Merle Travis**, after whom "Travis picking" is named, and
Chet Atkins spread it through country guitar. The 1960s folk revival brought it to singer-songwriters.
**John Prine** (1946-2020), the Chicago postman whose first album (*John Prine*, 1971) contains *Paradise*,
*Hello in There* and *Angel from Montgomery*, played a plain thumb-and-fingers style under plain-spoken songs.

## The band's version

- **Comping:** the *prine* and *travis* patterns. **Bass:** root and fifth with the thumb. **Drums:** none.

## Listening

| Recording | Year | Listen for |
|---|---|---|
| Mississippi John Hurt, *Candy Man Blues* | 1928 | Steady alternating thumb. |
| Merle Travis, *Cannonball Rag* | 1940s | Travis picking itself. |
| Elizabeth Cotten, *Freight Train* | late 1950s | The folk-revival classic. |
| John Prine, *Paradise* (*John Prine*) | 1971 | The style the band copies. |
| John Prine, *Angel from Montgomery* (*John Prine*) | 1971 | Thumb and fingers under a slow song. |

### More recent

| Recording | Year | Listen for |
|---|---|---|
| Jason Isbell, *Elephant* | 2013 | A fingerpicked song from one of Prine's heirs. |
| Taylor Swift, *invisible string* (*folklore*) | 2020 | Thumb-and-fingers guitar under a pop song. |
